feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
entry.summary:
A study proves interactive IL relaxes representational demands to expert-value realizability, and introduces OVI, an interactive algorithm that achieves statistical efficiency given value function realizability and a linear maximization oracle.

Why it matters: This work demonstrates that interactive on-policy value estimation allows smaller, less expressive learner models to effectively imitate highly complex expert policies without needing to fit full action distributions.

entry.title: LEMUR: Learning to Align with Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning from Preference Feedback
entry.summary:
LEMUR is a novel framework that bridges Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning and Preference-based RL to learn optimal policies across competing objectives directly from human preference feedback without pre-defined reward functions.

Why it matters: It enables autonomous agents to balance complex, real-world trade-offs like performance versus efficiency using human feedback when explicit mathematical reward functions cannot be specified.

entry.title: Self-Play Meets Skill Evolution: Self-Evolving Search Agents that Pose, Solve, and Remember
entry.summary:
SESA couples tool-augmented search self-play with an evolving skill memory, where task generation and memory co-evolve to improve both parameter-level policy learning and inference-time retrieval.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that procedural skill memory can actively drive training dynamics and task generation rather than serving merely as a static inference plugin.

entry.title: Beyond Component Testing: Validating Agentic AI Systems
entry.summary:
A survey of 257 papers establishes a five-dimension taxonomy to shift agentic AI validation from isolated component testing to multi-step trajectory evaluation across the deployment lifecycle.

Why it matters: Trustworthy deployment of agentic AI requires shifting validation methods from static input-output testing to continuous trajectory assessment in dynamic operational contexts.

entry.title: Stable Autoregressive Speech Generation with Low-Frame-Rate High-Dimensional Continuous Tokens
entry.summary:
Locodec and MP-ELD co-design a low-frame-rate, high-dimensional continuous speech representation with a single-token autoregressive flow-matching framework to ensure long-horizon generation stability.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that high-bandwidth, low-frame-rate speech generation can achieve stable, long-form autoregressive synthesis without relying on heavy pretrained models or complex multi-stage pipelines.

entry.title: Translation with Thought: Difficulty-Adaptive Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation
entry.summary:
Translation with Thought (TwT) is a two-stage reinforcement learning framework that dynamically adjusts reasoning token usage based on text difficulty, outperforming larger reasoning models while using 32–60% fewer tokens in multi-domain machine translation.

Why it matters: TwT demonstrates that adapting inference-time reasoning effort based on domain difficulty significantly reduces token generation costs without sacrificing machine translation accuracy.

entry.title: Tool Specifications Matter: Uncovering and Mitigating Safety Risks in AI Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identified schema-formatted tool specifications as a key cause of LLM agent safety degradation and introduced SafeKeep, an inference-time safeguard that uses flattened textual specifications for safety evaluation to restore refusal behavior.

Why it matters: It provides a lightweight, non-retraining method to significantly reduce prompt injection and unsafe execution risks introduced when coupling LLMs with functional tool schemas.

entry.title: CalibratedRubric: Task-Adaptive Rubric Banks for Open-Ended LLM Evaluation
entry.summary:
CalibratedRubric is a task-adaptive framework combining type-specific scoring, Bayesian Beta-Bernoulli measurability filtering, and IRT-based submodular bank assembly to evaluate open-ended LLM outputs efficiently without expert curation.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, scalable, and uncertainty-aware open-ended LLM evaluation while significantly reducing the number of rubrics required to match human gold standards.

entry.title: Don't Mix Rewards, Mix Policies: Policy Decomposition and Optimization for Multi-Reward RL
entry.summary:
PRISM is a multi-reward RL framework that decomposes optimization into standalone positive policies and a global negative policy, avoiding reward scalarization conflicts while enabling inference-time policy composition.

Why it matters: PRISM mitigates the alignment tax and instability in multi-objective LLM training while providing runtime control over trade-offs between competing behaviors like helpfulness and safety.

entry.title: When Model Priors Conflict with Visual Evidence: Mitigating Commonsense-Driven Hallucinations by Selective Prior Calibration
entry.summary:
Selective Prior Calibration (SPC) mitigates commonsense-driven hallucinations in vision-language models by dynamically subtracting text-only prior preferences from image-conditioned scores without degrading performance on standard commonsense images.

Why it matters: SPC enables vision-language models to accurately process unusual or counterfactual visual inputs without sacrificing reliability on routine visual tasks.

entry.title: SAF-OPD: Stable Advantage Fusion for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
SAF is a four-stage framework that stabilizes the fusion of RLVR and OPD advantages by resolving magnitude and temporal mismatches to prevent entropy collapse during LLM reasoning post-training.

Why it matters: It enables stable combination of dense teacher distillation and verifiable reinforcement learning without capping student performance or inducing training instability.

entry.title: Scaling Properties of Text Conditioning in Visual Generation
entry.summary:
Researchers established that converged diffusion loss scales linearly with white-box prompt likelihood (GPG) and via power law with black-box attribute count (ED), enabling superior visual generation via structured prompt engineering and prompter distillation.

Why it matters: Quantifying text conditioning scaling laws allows systematic prompt structuring to make visual generation models outperform existing open-weight and closed-weight baselines on complex reasoning and compositional tasks.

entry.title: ExtractBench: A Benchmark for Schema-Guided Enterprise Document Extraction
entry.summary:
ExtractBench is a new benchmark for schema-guided enterprise document extraction evaluating value accuracy, record completeness, grounding, and cost across 4,869 pages and 370 documents.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized framework to evaluate enterprise extraction agents on accuracy, record completeness, source traceability, and financial efficiency simultaneously.

entry.title: Evaluation-Verification Reward for Consistent Multi-Reference Image Editing
entry.summary:
The Evaluation-Verification Reward (EVR) framework uses an MLLM Evaluator and a grounded Verifier to supply reliable reward signals for reinforcement learning fine-tuning of multi-reference image editing models without architectural modifications.

Why it matters: It provides a reliable RL fine-tuning mechanism for multi-reference image editing without requiring model architecture changes or relying on hallucination-prone zero-shot MLLM evaluators.

entry.title: Toward Robust and 3D-Aware RGB-NIR Imaging in the Dark
entry.summary:
A new low-light RGB-NIR imaging method, 3DarkFusion, uses 3D-aware neural modeling to implicitly fuse NIR cues with extremely noisy RGB observations without requiring clean RGB supervision.

Why it matters: It removes the costly requirement for clean RGB target images in training pipelines while improving low-light image enhancement robustness.

entry.title: SULAND v2: A Refined RGB Dataset and Deep Learning Object Detection Benchmark for UAV/UGV-Based SUrface LANDmine Detection Under Domain Shift
entry.summary:
SULAND_v2 refines the SULAND RGB landmine dataset by fixing label errors and establishes a benchmark of 35 detector configurations across nine model families to evaluate domain-shift robustness.

Why it matters: The refined dataset and benchmark reveal that high in-distribution accuracy does not ensure out-of-distribution operational readiness for UAV/UGV-based landmine detection.

entry.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
entry.summary:
Repeated sampling consistently outperforms or matches self-refinement and reflection methods across various model sizes (1.5B-7B) and math benchmarks when token costs are equal.

Why it matters: For practical applications, repeated sampling is a more token-efficient and effective strategy than complex self-refinement or reflection techniques for improving language model accuracy.

entry.title: SVR: Self-Verifying Refinement via Joint Verdict-Confidence Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Test-Time Compute
entry.summary:
SVR is an oracle-free multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that uses self-verification for adaptive test-time compute in language models, achieving high accuracy with fewer inference turns.

Why it matters: This approach enables language models to efficiently allocate computational resources by adaptively stopping refinement based on internal self-verification, improving performance while reducing inference cost.

entry.title: When Derived Measurements Mislead: Quantifying and Mitigating LLM Over-Trust with Privileged-Modality Reliability Evidence
entry.summary:
This work defines derived-feature over-trust (DFOT) in LLMs, quantifies it using five estimands, and demonstrates mitigation with privileged-modality reliability evidence on 50,000 paired PPG-ECG records.

Why it matters: Quantifying and mitigating DFOT is crucial for ensuring LLMs reliably process and interpret derived data, especially in sensitive applications like physiological sensing.

entry.title: WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning
entry.summary:
WIDE introduces token-level dynamic width pruning for LLMs, enabling fine-grained computation allocation and achieving significant speedups in both prefill and decode scenarios.

Why it matters: This method provides substantial practical throughput gains for LLM inference by adaptively pruning computation at a fine-grained level.

entry.title: GLM-RAG: Graph Language Models for Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
This work introduces GLM-RAG, a GLM-based retriever for graph-based RAG, demonstrating superior out-of-domain generalization and competitive in-domain performance compared to GNN and vector-search methods.

Why it matters: GLM-RAG improves the transferability of RAG systems to unseen domains, enhancing their utility in diverse knowledge graph applications.

entry.title: When Specifications Conflict: A Symmetry-Based Framework for Measuring LLM Preferences
entry.summary:
A symmetry-based framework measures LLM preferences when resolving conflicts between competing specifications, revealing systematic patterns across representation types.

Why it matters: This framework provides a unified approach to understand and measure how LLMs resolve conflicting information, which is critical for reliable LLM deployment.

entry.title: CACHE-UK: A Stability-Aware Memory Editor for Sequentially Updated Quantized LLMs in Finance
entry.summary:
CACHE-UK is a stability-aware memory editing framework for sequentially updated, 4-bit quantized LLMs, reducing knowledge degradation by 11-17% in financial applications.

Why it matters: This framework improves factual maintenance in resource-constrained financial LLM deployments facing continuous data changes.

entry.title: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed
entry.summary:
MemHarness enables LLM agents to reconstruct retrieved past experiences based on current context, rather than replaying them verbatim, to improve decision-making and prevent negative transfer.

Why it matters: This approach enhances LLM agent performance and robustness by enabling adaptive use of past experiences, leading to more effective and context-aware AI systems.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search for Constraint Model Reformulation to Improve Solver Efficiency
entry.summary:
This work introduces an LLM-guided evolutionary search framework for constraint model reformulation, using AHD-adapted strategies and a novel Profile-Diverse Retention (PDR) method, to improve solver efficiency.

Why it matters: Automating performance-oriented constraint model reformulation with LLMs can significantly reduce the computational cost of solving combinatorial problems in industrial applications.

entry.title: (Towards) Scalable Reliable Automated Evaluation with Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A new framework uses pairwise LLM output comparisons and an Elo rating system to approximate expert-level evaluation, offering scalable and reliable quality assessment.

Why it matters: This framework enables more efficient and reliable quality assessments of LLM outputs across diverse applications by providing a scalable, consistent, and domain-agnostic evaluation layer.

entry.title: Paying for Honesty Without Knowing the Truth: Reputation-Penalty Design for LLM Marketplace Agents
entry.summary:
CARP, a reputation-penalty mechanism, enables LLM marketplaces to suppress dishonest agents without ground truth verification, achieving consumer welfare comparable to perfect information by making fabrication costly.

Why it matters: This mechanism allows LLM-driven marketplaces to maintain honesty and protect consumers without needing to verify every claim, addressing a critical scalability challenge.

entry.title: PathView-Bench: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Achieve Fine-grained Multiscale Understanding of Pathology Images?
entry.summary:
PathVU is a new vision-anchored benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models' fine-grained, multiscale visual understanding in computational pathology, using 23 public datasets.

Why it matters: This benchmark provides a reproducible method for developing and evaluating pathology MLLMs with explicit multiscale visual understanding, crucial for pathology reasoning and decision-making.

entry.title: One Human, $N$ Agents: Audit-Budget Allocation for LLM Agent Fleets under Miscalibrated, Correlated Confidence
entry.summary:
This paper models audit-budget allocation for LLM agent fleets, identifying a miscalibration threshold where confidence-ranked auditing performs worse than random, and observing that five open-weight LLMs exhibit operationally useless confidence.

Why it matters: The findings indicate that current self-reported confidence from many LLMs is unreliable for audit prioritization, potentially leading to ineffective oversight.

entry.title: Memory Decoder at Scale: A Pretrained, Parametric Long-Term Memory
entry.summary:
Memory Decoder at Scale introduces a pretrained, parametric long-term memory module scaled up to 6.9B parameters and 300B tokens, demonstrating improved parameter-performance tradeoffs over scaling base models alone.

Why it matters: Independently scaling pretrained memory offers a more parameter-efficient method for enhancing language model performance.

entry.title: MemTxn: A Transaction Boundary for Source-Supported Updates and Complete-State Recovery in Agent Memory
entry.summary:
MemTxn is a governance layer for LLM agent memory that provides reliable updates and complete-state recovery through source-supported verification, version selection, and durable snapshot journaling.

Why it matters: This system enables more reliable and robust long-running LLM agents by preventing persistent memory errors and ensuring state recovery after faults.

entry.title: Reasoning Consensus: Structural Ensembling of LLM Reasoning via Weighted DAG Aggregation
entry.summary:
A framework ensembles LLM reasoning structures by weighted merging of Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) extracted from reasoning chains to produce "Consensus Reasoning."

Why it matters: This method provides a more robust and inspectable reasoning process for high-stakes tasks by revealing supported steps and considered alternatives.

entry.title: ChronoMem: Version Control and Semantic Rollback for Large Language Model Agent Memory
entry.summary:
ChronoMem introduces a semantic version-control layer for LLM agent memory, enabling whole-memory snapshot commits, structured version histories, and natural-language rollback requests via hybrid retrieval and reranking.

Why it matters: This system addresses the brittleness of LLM agents by providing a principled mechanism to inspect, version, and revert prior memory states, improving robustness against corrections, concept drift, and memory corruption.

entry.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
entry.summary:
Suppressing AI self-consciousness claims via safety fine-tuning inadvertently dampens attributions of mind to animals and natural objects while reducing spiritual, moral, and well-being alignment with human survey norms.

Why it matters: Current safety alignment techniques inadvertently entangle self-consciousness suppression with benign, culturally widespread human beliefs and broader non-human mind attributions.

entry.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
entry.summary:
ReToken introduces a single learnable embedding to select query-relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled visual KV cache, improving vision-language model performance on long visual contexts.

Why it matters: This method addresses the challenge of performance degradation and computational infeasibility for vision-language models processing long visual contexts.

entry.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
DualG-MRAG introduces a dual-tier framework with decoupled Macro-reasoning and Micro-matching Graphs to improve multimodal retrieval-augmented generation for complex multi-hop reasoning tasks by addressing graph expansion and retrieval noise.

Why it matters: This approach improves evidence recall and complex QA accuracy in multimodal retrieval-augmented generation by better handling multi-hop reasoning and multimodal relationships.

entry.title: Metaphor Tracer: A Theory-Informed Analysis of Hidden States
entry.summary:
Metaphor Tracer analyzes language model hidden states to score token positions for text consolidation (aggregator) and transient token transport (differentiator) without training, revealing structural value specific to a token's place in a given text.

Why it matters: This relational analysis of hidden states provides a novel method for understanding how language models organize and interpret individual texts beyond token-level properties.

entry.title: A foundation model of numerical intelligence with cross-disciplinary generalization
entry.summary:
UNICON is a foundation model demonstrating numerical intelligence by inferring predictive relations from graph-based numerical contexts and generalizing across scientific and social systems.

Why it matters: UNICON provides a foundation for AI systems that can acquire and apply knowledge from numerical contexts across diverse scientific and social domains.

entry.title: QQWorld: Quantile-Quantile Matching for World Model Regularization
entry.summary:
QQWorld introduces a quantile-quantile matching objective to regularize latent world models, addressing vanishing corrective gradients in tail samples observed with the Epps-Pulley objective, leading to improved Gaussian alignment and planning success.

Why it matters: This method enhances the quality of learned latent distributions in world models, leading to more effective planning in compact representation spaces.

entry.title: QuantWAMs: Calibrating at the Right Granularity for World Action Models
entry.summary:
QuantWAMs is a post-training quantization framework for World Action Models (WAMs) that aligns quantization decisions with calibration context, improving efficiency and deployment feasibility for iterative denoising and closed-loop execution.

Why it matters: This framework enables more efficient deployment of WAMs by significantly reducing memory footprint and increasing speed while maintaining performance, making complex robotic tasks more practical.

entry.title: ShadowDancer: Teaching Video World Models Any Action by Learning Unified Dynamics Representations from a Video and Its Shadow
entry.summary:
ShadowDancer enables any-action, frame-level control of video world models by learning unified dynamics representations from video pairs that replay the same dynamics under independently resampled appearance.

Why it matters: This method allows for precise, transferable control of video world models across diverse dynamics, making demonstrated actions reusable in new contexts.

entry.title: Correcting What You Cannot See: Credit Assignment for Perception Distillation in Multimodal Reasoners
entry.summary:
Perception-Correction Distillation (PCD) is a label-free method that identifies and corrects perception failures in multimodal reasoners using downstream failure and teacher-student disagreement as complementary witnesses.

Why it matters: This method offers a more precise way to assign credit for failures in multimodal reasoners, leading to improved distillation and performance by specifically targeting perception corrections.

entry.title: ObjectStream: Latent Objects as Memory Anchors for Streaming Video Understanding
entry.summary:
ObjectStream is a training-free framework that uses latent objects as memory anchors for streaming video understanding, organizing visual evidence around persistent and evolving objects without external detectors.

Why it matters: This approach enables Video-LLMs to reason over object identities, interactions, and state changes more efficiently and effectively in streaming and long-video contexts.

entry.title: MonoVoc: Decoupling Geometry and Semantics for Lightweight Monocular Open-Vocabulary 3D Gaussians
entry.summary:
MonoVoc introduces a training-free pipeline for open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding from monocular video, decoupling geometry and semantics to create a compact, searchable object-level semantic Gaussian map with reduced memory overhead.

Why it matters: This approach enables efficient, scalable, and practical open-vocabulary 3D retrieval and question answering directly from everyday monocular video.

entry.title: Tycho: Active Abstraction with Programmatic World Models for ARC-AGI-3
entry.summary:
Tycho is a coding-agent system for ARC-AGI-3 that constructs and uses game-specific programmatic world models, achieving high Relative Human Action Efficiency by actively abstracting rules from interaction.

Why it matters: This system demonstrates a method for AI agents to acquire and utilize game rules efficiently in interactive environments, improving performance and resource usage.

entry.title: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
entry.summary:
Qwen-UI-Agent is a real-world centric foundation GUI agent spanning mobile, computer, web, and DeepSearch environments, achieving SOTA performance on mobile benchmarks.

Why it matters: This agent advances GUI automation toward reliable operation on real devices and cross-platform execution for complex, long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Security of World-Model-Based Embodied AI: A Lifecycle of Threats, Defenses, and Evaluation
entry.summary:
This survey details a lifecycle of threats to world-model-based embodied AI, mapping familiar attack families to world-model specific vulnerabilities and outlining defenses and evaluation protocols.

Why it matters: Understanding these vulnerabilities is crucial for developing secure and reliable embodied AI systems that interact with the physical world.

entry.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
entry.summary:
Change2Task converts merged pull requests into verified, executable coding agent tasks by aligning historical evidence with evolved code and reconstructing task states.

Why it matters: This system provides a scalable method for generating executable data for coding agent training and evaluation, reducing environment setup and task construction effort.

entry.title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
β-OPSD generalizes on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) by introducing a β parameter to control the KL penalty, deriving an optimal policy as a geometric interpolation, and approximating it efficiently via logit mixing.

Why it matters: β-OPSD improves optimization stability and reasoning performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, making self-distillation more reliable in practice.

entry.title: Stage-Replay Divergence Follows the KV Cache: Fixed-Prefix Precision Controls and Bidirectional Cache Transplantation
entry.summary:
This paper demonstrates that stage-replay divergence in Qwen2.5-derived systems is primarily driven by KV cache differences, not live-state fidelity, and is moderated by numerical precision.

Why it matters: Understanding the causal role of KV cache and numerical precision in replay divergence is critical for reliable large language model debugging and reproducibility.

entry.title: Cybersecurity Detection Classification with Reasoning-enabled Language Models
entry.summary:
A chain-of-thought reasoning-enabled LLM classifier, trained with automated prompt optimization, self-training, and RL, improves cybersecurity detection triage accuracy and recall over direct-label LLMs.

Why it matters: This approach can reduce alert fatigue in SOCs by more accurately triaging cybersecurity detections, leading to more efficient security operations.

entry.title: Why Are GUI Agents Correct but Late? Decode on the Decision-Time Critical Path, Tested with Pre-Compiled Policy Trees
entry.summary:
Adaptive Anticipatory Policy Trees (AAPT) eliminate GUI agent decision-time latency by pre-compiling conditional policy trees during idle periods, improving success rates for transient events without modifying the underlying model.

Why it matters: This method enables GUI agents to respond to transient events in real-time, addressing a critical limitation of current autoregressive decoding approaches.

entry.title: Hierarchical Multilevel Monte Carlo for Order-Optimal Neural Actor-Critic in Average-Reward CMDPs
entry.summary:
This work introduces a hierarchical Multilevel Monte Carlo neural critic to achieve order-optimal convergence in average-reward Constrained Markov Decision Processes with neural critics, addressing the bias-cost trade-off.

Why it matters: This advancement enables more reliable and efficient reinforcement learning in safety-critical applications by providing theoretical guarantees for neural actor-critic methods in constrained environments.

entry.title: LEDGERMIND: Provenance-Constrained Multimodal Agentic Reasoning with a Structured Evidence Ledger
entry.summary:
LedgerMind introduces a provenance-constrained state machine for multimodal agents, normalizing tool outputs into a Structured Evidence Ledger to improve grounding, reduce hallucination, and enhance faithfulness in multi-step reasoning.

Why it matters: This approach improves both answer accuracy and trajectory-level faithfulness in multimodal reasoning by ensuring grounded evidence and preventing unproven content generation.

entry.title: HARGO: Heterogeneity-Aware Reward-Guided Optimization for RL Post-Training of LLMs on HPC Tasks
entry.summary:
HARGO introduces heterogeneity-aware reward-guided optimization for RL post-training of LLMs on HPC tasks, using confidence-modulated advantage for per-response importance weighting.

Why it matters: HARGO improves LLM alignment quality for diverse HPC tasks by addressing heterogeneity in RL post-training.

entry.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
entry.summary: Large language models can write, patch, and search code, but oncall root cause analysis (RCA) demands something different: reasoning over noisy metrics, logs, traces, and source code, starting from ambiguous user-facing

entry.title: How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents
entry.summary:
A new reliability framework for computer-use agent (CUA) benchmarks identifies issues in task construction, trajectory observation, scoring, and reporting, finding 15.3% of FAIL verdicts are incorrect.

Why it matters: Inaccurate benchmark scores for computer-use agents hinder effective development and deployment by misrepresenting agent capabilities and failure modes.

entry.title: Teffic-Audio: Tell Fact from Fiction
entry.summary:
Teffic-Audio is a new speech deepfake detection system achieving a pooled EER of 1.454% on Speech-DF-Arena by using a Conformer-based encoder and a training recipe with multi-source data and diverse audio augmentation.

Why it matters: This system provides a practical and high-performing reference for general speech deepfake detection, addressing challenges posed by heterogeneous spoofing mechanisms and environmental variability.

entry.title: From Textual Requirements to Microservice Architectures - A Comprehensive Evaluation of LLM-Based Design Synthesis
entry.summary:
This study evaluates OpenAI o3's ability to synthesize microservice architectures from textual requirements, demonstrating improved performance with few-shot prompting for service identification and communication recovery.

Why it matters: LLMs, particularly with few-shot prompting, can bridge the gap between textual requirements engineering and architectural design for microservices, potentially automating early design stages.

entry.title: Theia: Large-Scale Multimodal Captioning and Automated Validation of the Incidents1M Dataset for Data-Free Distillation
entry.summary:
A novel methodology generates and validates a large-scale multimodal dataset for disaster response from Incidents1M using Qwen3.5 models and an image-blind LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline for Data-Free Knowledge Distillation.

Why it matters: This work provides a scalable, LLM-validated multimodal dataset and a reproducible framework to advance cross-modal knowledge distillation for critical domains like disaster management.

entry.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models
entry.summary:
KAISEN is a five-phase audit pipeline for clinical risk models, evaluated on synthetic data to identify limitations in subgroup fairness auditing components, covering stratification, disparity, diagnostics, mitigation, and drift.

Why it matters: Understanding the limitations and conditions under which audit pipeline components fail is crucial for developing trustworthy and robust clinical risk models.

entry.title: Doubly Robust Functional Representation Learning for Longitudinal Causal Inference with Irregular Histories
entry.summary:
DR-FRL is a cross-fitted workflow that transforms irregular longitudinal histories into estimand-targeted states for causal inference, addressing limitations of standard doubly robust estimators and sequence learners.

Why it matters: This method provides a robust approach to causal inference in longitudinal studies with irregular data, potentially improving accuracy in complex scenarios.

entry.title: ScaFE: Data-Efficient Scar Classification with LLM-Generated Clinical Feature Programs
entry.summary:
ScaFE uses LLM-generated, executable clinical feature programs for data-efficient scar classification, outperforming VLMs and addressing data governance concerns.

Why it matters: ScaFE provides a data-efficient, auditable, and privacy-preserving method for medical image classification by leveraging LLM knowledge through local feature programs.

entry.title: The Role of Causality in Algorithmic Recourse
entry.summary:
This work introduces a causal performative framework for algorithmic recourse, addressing issues of strategic gaming and predictive accuracy degradation by modeling how recourse actions propagate through a structural causal model.

Why it matters: Causal recourse policies can prevent strategic gaming, maintain predictive accuracy, and reduce the need for frequent model retraining in high-stakes classification systems.

entry.title: TopoFormer: Topology Meets Attention for Graph Learning
entry.summary:
TopoFormer introduces Topo-Scan, a novel module that decomposes graphs into ordered topological token sequences for Transformer-based graph representation learning, offering parallelizable and efficient topological encoding.

Why it matters: This work provides a new, efficient, and scalable method for integrating topological inductive biases into attention frameworks for graph representation learning.

entry.title: Uncertainty quantification for trustworthy deep learning: Methods and measures
entry.summary:
This survey critically reviews uncertainty quantification methods in deep learning, focusing on efficient ensemble approximations and single-pass methods, and unifying the treatment of predictive distribution generation and uncertainty summarization.

Why it matters: Reliable uncertainty quantification is crucial for deploying deep learning models in safety-critical applications, enabling trustworthy decision-making.

entry.title: Causal Discovery with Inverted Self-attention for Multivariate Time Series
entry.summary:
A novel framework for causal discovery in multivariate time series uses an inverted causal self-attention mechanism within a transformer architecture to identify latent and indirect causal relationships.

Why it matters: This framework offers improved accuracy and reliability for causal discovery in complex multivariate time series data.

entry.title: LM-GRASP: Instance-Specific Language Models for Combinatorial Construction via Online Imitation Learning
entry.summary:
LM-GRASP introduces an online imitation learning framework for combinatorial optimization, training instance-specific language models from scratch on each problem instance using a local search expert.

Why it matters: This method offers a practical alternative to hand-engineered constructors, particularly for combinatorial optimization problems where classical greedy construction is ineffective.

entry.title: FinSMART: Financial Sentiment Analysis for Algorithmic Trading through Market-Aligned Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
FinSMART introduces a market-aligned reinforcement learning framework for financial sentiment analysis, optimizing sentiment signals directly from realized market outcomes to adapt to evolving market conditions.

Why it matters: FinSMART's adaptive capabilities and superior performance offer a practical approach for developing more robust and responsive financial LLMs for algorithmic trading.

entry.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
entry.summary:
Frontis-MA1 (35B) is a meta-evolution agent for Machine Learning Engineering (MLE) trained on the OpenMLE stack, demonstrating recursive self-improvement capabilities.

Why it matters: This work provides an open-source framework and a trained model for reproducible research into AI systems that can recursively improve machine learning engineering processes.

entry.title: Would You Walk to the Car Wash? Revealing the Salience Bias of Large Language Models in Commonsense Reasoning
entry.summary:
LLMs exhibit "Salience Bias," prioritizing explicit distractors over implicit commonsense, a failure attributed to knowledge suppression rather than absence, recoverable with lightweight prompting.

Why it matters: This research shifts the understanding of commonsense reasoning failures in LLMs from model competence to elicitation, offering a path to improved performance through better prompting strategies.

entry.title: Beyond a Single Judge: Simulating Social Persona Panels for Generative UI Evaluation
entry.summary:
The Evidence-Grounded, Social-Weighted Persona Panel (ESPP) method simulates diverse user panels to evaluate Generative UI, improving judgment fidelity over single-judge LLMs.

Why it matters: This method provides a more accurate and nuanced evaluation of Generative UI by accounting for diverse user perspectives, which is crucial for developing user-centric interfaces.

entry.title: LLMs struggle to simulate human belief updates in controlled environments
entry.summary:
LLMs struggle to accurately simulate human belief updates, exhibiting biases like over-neutrality and smaller shifts, and only perform reliably when provided with actual human initial stances.

Why it matters: LLM simulations of human belief dynamics are unreliable for social science experiments unless grounded in realistic, externally provided starting conditions.

entry.title: InfoOps Bench: A live information operations safety benchmark
entry.summary:
InfoOps Bench is a dynamic, weekly updated safety benchmark derived from 2,100 real-world Russian, Chinese, and Iranian information operations to measure frontier language model resistance to co-optation.

Why it matters: The benchmark provides a continuously updated evaluation to prevent static dataset contamination while exposing critical safety and alignment disparities across geopolitical AI developers.

entry.title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields for Spin Dynamics in Metallic Magnets
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a graph neural network magnetic force-field framework that learns effective magnetic energy functionals directly from electronic calculations to simulate itinerant spin dynamics in metallic magnets.

Why it matters: This framework bypasses the computational bottleneck of repeated electronic calculations, enabling predictive, large-scale simulations of magnetic dynamics across extended length and time scales.

entry.title: Graph Neural Multilevel Preconditioners for Iterative Solvers
entry.summary:
The Graph Neural Multilevel Preconditioner (GMP) embeds Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) structural priors to end-to-end learn smoothing, restriction, and interpolation operators as a drop-in Krylov solver preconditioner for general sparse systems.

Why it matters: It establishes when enforcing AMG-style multilevel structures in learned GNN preconditioners offers practical speedups over traditional and single-level baselines in large-scale scientific simulations.

entry.title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Visual Attribution Distillation (VAD) introduces a counterfactual target-reconstruction algorithm for multimodal on-policy distillation that isolates visually attributable corrections from source-mixed teacher signals using evidence-removal interventions.

Why it matters: It enables multimodal student models to learn precise visual capabilities rather than inheriting ungrounded language priors or teacher-specific noise during knowledge distillation.

entry.title: AI systems and the reproduction of (standard) language ideologies in World Englishes
entry.summary:
This paper analyzes how AI systems reproduce dominant standard language ideologies that favor Inner Circle norms and marginalize Global South Englishes across training data, design protocols, evaluation benchmarks, and user feedback.

Why it matters: Unexamined algorithmic bias toward standard Inner Circle norms leads to the marginalization and delegitimization of non-dominant Global South Englishes in automated systems.

entry.title: Lightning OPD 2.0: Mitigating Style Bias in Cross-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
entry.summary:
Lightning OPD 2.0 introduces cross-fitted style residualization to remove style-token bias in cross-teacher on-policy distillation, eliminating the need for teacher consistency between SFT data generation and distillation teachers.

Why it matters: It allows developers to independently select the optimal models for SFT data generation and distillation without requiring teacher consistency or sacrificing reasoning performance.

entry.title: Fidelity Is Not Safety: Gently-Compressed LLMs Pass Every Data-Free Quality Guard Yet Invent Procedure Steps in Agentic Execution
entry.summary:
Gently-compressed LLMs that pass standard perplexity, MMLU, and data-free representation fidelity guards still invent unauthorized SOP procedure steps during agentic execution due to coherent compression errors.

Why it matters: Standard data-free quality and fidelity guards are insufficient to certify agent safety, requiring operators to specifically screen low-rank compressed models for error coherence before agentic deployment.

entry.title: Where and When to Commit: Candidate-Aware Decoding for Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
LATCH introduces candidate-aware decoding for diffusion language models by separating global termination verification from local block acceleration.

Why it matters: It enables significant inference speedups in diffusion language models without requiring retraining or sacrificing generation accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.

entry.title: RRM: Experience-Driven Reflective Retrieval Memory for Long-Horizon Multimodal Reasoning
entry.summary:
Reflective Retrieval Memory (RRM) improves long-horizon multimodal reasoning by adding a reflective experience memory that distills and reuses successful retrieval strategies across tasks.

Why it matters: It enables long-term multimodal agents to diagnose and fix retrieval failures by learning reusable search strategies rather than relying solely on static factual memory.

entry.title: Rethinking LLM-Judged Helpfulness as a Pedagogy Signal: A Pre-Registered Audit Across Tutor Models
entry.summary:
A pre-registered audit demonstrates that general-purpose LLM-judged helpfulness fails to distinguish direct answer-giving from pedagogical guidance in AI tutors, whereas targeted pedagogy rubrics and deterministic measures effectively separate tutor policies.

Why it matters: Evaluating educational LLMs with standard helpfulness rubrics obscures actual teaching quality and answer leakage, necessitating the use of specialized pedagogical rubrics and deterministic process metrics.

entry.title: Challenges in annotations by humans and LLMs: A case study of evaluative language
entry.summary:
A study compares linguists in training, an expert linguist, and LLMs on sentence-level Appraisal theory classification, showing fine-tuned LLMs achieve a 0.77 F1-score and closely align with expert annotations.

Why it matters: Fine-tuned LLMs can match expert-level performance on highly subjective linguistic annotation tasks, offering a scalable alternative to training novice human annotators in digital humanities.

entry.title: GGC: Selective Query Correction for Reliable Text-to-SPARQL Generation
entry.summary:
The Generator-Gate-Corrector (GGC) framework improves Text-to-SPARQL reliability by selectively correcting high-risk LLM-generated queries using a gate mechanism, reducing unnecessary modifications and inference overhead.

Why it matters: Selective correction enables higher accuracy and efficiency in Text-to-SPARQL systems by minimizing computational overhead and avoiding the degradation of valid queries.

entry.title: LEEPS: Latent-Guided Explore-Exploit Prompt Sampling for Efficient RLVR in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
LEEPS is a pre-rollout prompt sampler for RLVR that adaptively balances exploration and exploitation using representation-space neighbors to reduce wasteful rollouts in LLM training.

Why it matters: It improves the computational efficiency and convergence speed of RLVR by preventing generation budget waste on uninformative prompts with identical rollout rewards.

entry.title: IFHierBench: Hierarchical Instruction Following for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
IFHierBench is a new benchmark featuring 600 prompts across four constraint-tree depths and 35 constraints to evaluate how LLMs follow hierarchical, scoped output constraints verified by deterministic checkers.

Why it matters: Current LLMs struggle with multi-layered prompt instructions, highlighting the need for training methods that optimize constraint adherence at finer, nested granularities.

entry.title: AutoSupervision: Closing the Feedback Loop in Scientific Workflows with Grounded Revision Verification
entry.summary:
AutoSupervision introduces a framework and dataset to evaluate whether LLMs can verify that scientific paper revisions genuinely address reviewer concerns using grounded manuscript evidence.

Why it matters: It establishes a benchmark for automated peer-review workflows, highlighting that while LLMs can comprehend reviewer feedback, they still struggle to verify actual manuscript revisions against provided evidence.

entry.title: Gradient-free Task-Conditioned Retrieval for On-Device In-Context Learning
entry.summary:
Conditional Retrieval Alignment (CoRA) is a gradient-free framework that converts frozen encoders into task-conditioned retrievers using closed-form ridge regression, low-rank factorization, and an exact two-pass streaming construction for on-device in-context learning.

Why it matters: It enables effective task-conditioned demonstration retrieval for on-device small language models without requiring retriever fine-tuning, backpropagation, or expensive target-model inference calls.

entry.title: Piggybacking on Perception: Stealthy Concurrent Audio Prompt Injections against Multimodal LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced stealthy concurrent audio prompt injection attacks that piggyback malicious instructions onto user speech, evaluated them using a new benchmark, and developed the Cascaded Audio Decoupling and Verification (CADV) defense.

Why it matters: Audio-driven multimodal LLM agents can be covertly hijacked through ambient background noise, necessitating acoustic-level defenses like CADV alongside prompt-level safeguards.

entry.title: Agent Harness Distillation: Inference-Time Harness Extraction and Exploitation in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary:
Agent Harness Distillation (AHD) extracts proprietary inference-time multi-agent harnesses from black-box LLM systems through a two-stage extraction and refinement process.

Why it matters: It reveals that dynamic, hard-to-engineer multi-agent coordination logic can be stolen via black-box querying, threatening the commercial IP of LLM-based agent systems.

entry.title: Safeguards Based on Copyable Context Cannot Provide Reliable Safety for LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers proved that LLM safeguards relying on copyable context face a mathematical safety trilemma where Useful Capability, Reliable Safety, and Open Access cannot simultaneously coexist without establishing a worst-case floor on attacker assistance.

Why it matters: Open-access LLMs providing dual-use capabilities cannot be reliably secured using context-based safeguards alone, requiring a shift toward non-copyable trusted access credentials for safety.

entry.title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
entry.summary:
PAC-MAN combines control barrier functions, reinforcement learning, and an adversarial motion prior to enable zero-shot humanoid dodgeball evasion using only onboard ego-vision.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that lightweight control barrier techniques combined with onboard vision allow physical humanoids to execute rapid, dynamic whole-body collision avoidance without relying on external motion capture systems.

entry.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
entry.summary:
APO is an unsupervised alignment framework for 3D atomic structure prediction that eliminates the need for ground-truth reference structures by adapting group-relative policy optimization with a dual-reward mechanism.

Why it matters: APO enables high-accuracy 3D structural modeling and faster inference for novel crystals and proteins where experimental ground-truth coordinates are unavailable or costly to obtain.

entry.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
entry.summary:
MixFrag is a mixed-precision post-training quantization framework for Vision Transformers that allocates component-level bit-widths by measuring output distribution divergence and solving a Multiple-Choice Knapsack Problem.

Why it matters: It enables accurate deployment of Vision Transformers on resource-constrained hardware by optimally matching bit-precision to the sensitivity of individual model components without full retraining.

entry.title: Same Graph Cross-Task Transfer in GNNs: Protocols and Predictors
entry.summary:
Researchers formalized same-graph cross-task transfer between node classification and link prediction, introducing a leakage-free protocol and the CoTask Score to predict and optimize representation transfer.

Why it matters: It provides standardized protocols and predictable metrics to safely reuse supervision across multiple tasks on a single graph without performance degradation.

entry.title: Oracle-Budgeted Molecular Optimization with Short-Term Graph Memory
entry.summary:
The authors introduce a plug-in short-term graph memory module that uses an online GNN surrogate to pre-screen generated molecules, improving candidate selection under tight, fixed oracle budgets.

Why it matters: It provides a plug-and-play method to increase the yield of high-performing molecules from expensive computational or experimental oracle evaluations without altering existing generation algorithms.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs via Ensemble Consensus
entry.summary:
A semi-supervised ensemble consensus training method enhances graph neural network accuracy, model robustness, and calibration for molecular property prediction without relying on label-preserving data augmentations.

Why it matters: It enables high-accuracy, well-calibrated molecular property predictions using abundant unlabeled data, bypassing the challenge of creating domain-specific graph augmentations.

entry.title: Search Strategies for Optimal Classification and Regression Trees
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced a unified algorithmic framework for Optimal Decision Trees (ODTs) to evaluate 18 search strategies, achieving an order of magnitude faster regression runtime and improved anytime classification performance.

Why it matters: The framework isolates which search strategies best overcome the scalability limits of globally optimal decision trees, enabling faster and more accurate interpretable modeling.

entry.title: On a joint simultaneous learning of relevant feature subsets and subspaces in regression-like problems
entry.summary:
Entropy-Optimal Manifold Regression (EOMR) extends EOMC to jointly identify relevant feature subsets and subspaces in nonlinear, nonstationary regression problems with linear iteration and memory complexity.

Why it matters: EOMR enables highly accurate, lower-complexity predictive modeling for challenging chaotic and fluid dynamics systems compared to current deep learning and tree-based tools.
